meta.scene_summary: Big Tech is busy building the data center of the future while the rest of us are just trying to figure out who broke the sandbox.

cooking.headline: AMD is officially breaking up with your gaming PC to date the data center
cooking.summary: AMD just told gamers that the server rack is their new priority and consumer PCs are basically a side project. It's the hardware version of your friend who gets a new partner and suddenly stops showing up to game night.
cooking.plain_english: AMD has announced that it will prioritize its data center business over consumer computer sales, as it expects a significant decline in the personal computer market.

cooking.headline: Google is buying data center land in Wyoming because the cloud needs to live somewhere
cooking.summary: Google just bought a massive data center site in Wyoming, proving they are fully committed to the real estate side of the AI arms race. Apparently, you can't just host the future of intelligence on a thumb drive in a garage anymore.
cooking.plain_english: Google has purchased a property in Wyoming previously owned by Crusoe Energy to expand its data center infrastructure.

cooking.headline: GitHub is finally rearranging the furniture in its storage closet
cooking.summary: GitHub is overhauling how it stores your code to handle the sheer weight of everyone's 'final_final_v2' commits. It turns out even the world's biggest repository needs a spring cleaning to keep from buckling under the pressure of our collective technical debt.
cooking.plain_english: GitHub has updated its internal system for storing and managing Git data to improve performance and scalability.

cooking.headline: Replit is putting your code in a smaller, more expensive glass box
cooking.summary: Replit rebuilt its sandbox using microVMs, which is essentially giving every line of your code its own tiny, isolated apartment. It is the perfect solution for when your experimental project inevitably tries to break the entire building.
cooking.plain_english: Replit has updated its platform to use micro-virtual machines, which improves security and isolation for code running in its browser-based environment.

cooking.headline: Perplexity just turned your search engine into a group project
cooking.summary: Perplexity is launching autonomous agents to handle complex workflows, essentially automating the part of your job that involves waiting for someone else to reply. It's a bold move to fix productivity, assuming you enjoy managing AI staff as much as you enjoy managing human ones.
cooking.plain_english: Perplexity has introduced software agents that can independently perform multi-step work tasks for users.

cooked.headline: Corporate America is learning that political favors have a very short expiration date
cooked.summary: After betting big on a political shift, these tech giants are now discovering that congressional subpoenas are the default tax for being relevant. It is the corporate equivalent of realizing your 'get out of jail free' card was actually just a coupon for a salad.
cooked.plain_english: Several major technology companies are facing official investigations from members of the United States Congress.

cooked.headline: Microsoft and Oracle are breaking up, and it's definitely 'it's not you, it's my own AI cloud'
cooked.summary: Microsoft is ending its deal to rent Oracle's cloud capacity now that their own GPU clusters are finally ready for prime time. It turns out that relying on your frenemy for infrastructure is only a phase until you build your own backyard server farm.
cooked.plain_english: Microsoft is discontinuing its agreement to use Oracle's cloud services to support its artificial intelligence operations as its own data center capacity increases.

cooked.headline: Slickdeals got hacked, so maybe hold off on that 'too good to be true' discount
cooked.summary: The site dedicated to finding the lowest prices has officially been compromised, proving that even the best deals come with a security catch. It's the digital equivalent of finding a bargain bin item that turns out to be a tracking device.
cooked.plain_english: The coupon and deal website Slickdeals has experienced a security breach involving unauthorized access to their systems.

cooked.headline: Firecracker just learned that 'sandboxing' is more of a suggestion than a rule.
cooked.summary: The minimalist VM designed to be the ultimate fortress for serverless functions just got hit with a breakout exploit. It turns out even your high-security hypervisor can be tricked into letting a guest escape if you ask it the right questions.
cooked.plain_english: A security vulnerability was discovered that allows software running inside a Firecracker virtual machine to escape its confines and access the host system.

cooked.headline: RealPage found out that algorithmic price fixing is just a cartel with better branding.
cooked.summary: The company used an algorithm to help landlords coordinate rent hikes, effectively turning the housing market into a giant group project where everyone cheats. Turns out the courts don't consider 'it was the AI's idea' a valid legal defense for price gouging.
cooked.plain_english: RealPage has agreed to pay $360 million to settle a lawsuit alleging that its software was used to help landlords collude to keep rental prices artificially high.
